name: X Couloir (Southwest Face) / Standard Route

text.approach: The X Couloir is most directly approached from the south via the Middle Fork Nooksack River Road (FR-38); the less direct alternative starts at Heliotrope Ridge and reaches the southwest face through the Thunder Glacier cirque. Drive FR-38 toward its mile-12.5 switchback and start hiking/bushwhacking the old decommissioned road around Pt. 4481 toward Rankin Creek — snow travel (often by bike or snowshoe on the lower stretch) leads past East Rankin Lake (~5,120 ft) and up into the basin to a sheltered camp at treeline around 6,100 ft, near the highest trees in the basin below Seward Peak. From camp, an alpine start gets the team into the southwest basin and across the bergschrund crux while it's still cold and firm, climbing roughly 1,500 ft of 30-40° snow and a steep serac step in the X Couloir to the 9,085 ft summit. Total approach is on the order of 7 miles and 3,350 ft of gain to the basin camp. Important — access note: FR-38 (Middle Fork Nooksack River Road), damaged in the December 2025 floods, has been closed to vehicles at milepost 7 by a washout since 27 July 2026, with no end date given on the Mt. text.overview: Lincoln Peak's SW Face route, known as the 'X Couloir' (sometimes referenced as 'X Couloir – Emancipation Proclamation'), is the historic line up this seldom-climbed, seriously loose Black Buttes summit. First climbed by Fred Beckey, Wesley Grande, John Rupley, and Herb Staley on July 22, 1956, it was the only documented route to the summit until a 2015 first ascent opened a second line on the NW Face. Only about a dozen ascents are known; the peak is guarded by near-vertical walls on every side
text.descent: Most parties reverse the ascent line, downclimbing and rappelling the same southwest gully/couloir system (the X Couloir) back down into the southwest basin below the face. This is a real rappelling descent, not a walk-off: the most detailed documented descent (a repeat/'2nd descent' trip report) describes 10 double-rope rappels — 4 off pickets placed by the descending party, 1 off a sling around
